title: Rules Are Rules
subtitle: What could be more pressing than the work right in front of us?

branch.text: Just a head, no creepy black bones sticking out from your temples?
Thank goodness. I'm not sure I could handle another conversation with those lunatics.
I do hope, if you ever find a bone stuck through your brain one day, that you won't hesitate to see a doctor.
But why bother covering such a pretty face? You're young and good-looking.
Don't be so shy to show it off. If that boneheaded lunatic doesn't bother to hide her face, you shouldn't either.
But seriously, if you do find a bone stuck through your brain one day, don't hesitate to see a doctor.
I don't call that woman a lunatic without good reason.
I doubt I would survive it
So you say, but you know what happened to her: she died and came back.
That is a rare privilege. How many can say they had the same gift? Death tends to be terribly final for most.
She was the exception, and just look at what she's made of it.
Life is pain. Lately it seems like every bone in my body aches ... Worse, the pain seems to come no matter the weather.
But I wasn't rewarded with immortality for all my pains.
It seems unfair that a privilege like that should be given to such a troublemaker.
This whole damned world is coming to an end!

items.text: Rules Are Rules
Foundation Office

items.speaker: Operation Team Leader I
items.text: No comms from the First Squad?
"Razor" catches the bad news as he enters their makeshift command post. His brow furrows beneath his mask as he surveys the room.
Several familiar squad captains are present, as well as the one who summoned them—Ms. Stranger—now standing before a desk.

items.speaker: "Razor"
items.text: Oh, everyone's here.

items.speaker: Operation Team Leader II
items.text: Over here, "Razor." We've just started.

items.speaker: "Razor"
items.text: Don't mind me. You were talking about the First Squad? They were the ones sent to the SPDM, right?

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Dispatch has lost contact with them. We're not sure whether they're in danger or if communication has been jammed by the "Storm."

items.speaker: Operation Team Leader II
items.text: Will we send another unit?

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: No. Dispatch has decided we can't risk sending anyone else with the "Storm" arriving so soon.
Though the piecemeal tactic is ultimately rejected, the captains in attendance know better than to openly defy their superiors.

items.speaker: "Razor"
items.text: Is there any clearer reason why they made that decision?

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: We can't risk leaving headquarters short-handed if an emergency breaks out. Besides, mobilizing another unit could easily spark panic among the people being processed.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Dispatch has determined that if we cannot make contact, it'll be better to deploy after the "Storm" has passed.

items.speaker: Operation Team Leader II
items.text: Then what are we here for, Ms. Stranger?

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Your teams will be performing reconnaissance in force as soon as the "Storm" ends. You are to gather any intel about the status of the First Squad and SPDM as soon as possible. I need you to prepare your teams in advance.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: But let me be clear. The purpose of this mission and the status of the SPDM and First Squad are on a need-to-know basis. You are not permitted to inform the lower ranks at this time.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: We have to take into account the possibility that some of your newer team members may act on impulse if they hear the news, especially the arcanists among them.

items.speaker: "Razor"
items.text: That's fair. I'm not sure I could hold some of them back from rushing into the "Storm" if they thought they could help.

items.speaker: "Razor"
items.text: For the good of the operation, we'll keep our mouths shut. Human or arcanist, we need to prioritize our teams' well-being.

items.speaker: Operation Team Leader I
items.text: Osborn's team will be fine. They have numbers, skills, and the latest gear. The Manus won't take them out—not without a fight.

items.speaker: Operation Team Leader I
items.text: I bet they'll be crowd surfing above the cheering students by the time we get to the SPDM.

items.speaker: Operation Team Leader II
items.text: Ms. Stranger, I've kept an eye on Team Timekeeper as ordered. I wouldn't say they're the most disciplined group, but they're doing fine.

items.speaker: Operation Team Leader II
items.text: Except the one that claims to be some kind of pirate-rockstar-come-freedom fighter. She's been selling the others on an escape plan.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: "Razor," could I ask you to speak to Regulus? You saved her life once on the Aegean. Perhaps she'll listen to you.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Here are your mission briefings: Keep them secret; keep them safe.
She hands each of the assembled captains a file.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Please follow Dispatch's instructions and report in before you make further decisions. You have your orders. Dismissed.
The other captains take their leave, and Ms. Stranger prepares to follow.

items.speaker: "Razor"
items.text: Wait, Ms. Stranger.
Registration Desk, St. Pavlov Foundation

items.speaker: Soldier I
items.text: What? I have to leave my things behind?
A soldier in a tattered uniform stands before the registration counter, a large bag set down beside him.

items.speaker: Registrar
items.text: Those are the rules, sir.

items.speaker: Registrar
items.text: I believe you've been informed that each individual is allowed only a maximum of 20 kilograms. Any excess baggage must be discarded unless it qualifies as military equipment.

items.speaker: Registrar
items.text: Since there is no military equipment in your baggage and ... You know what? I don't have time for this. Don't you see the line behind you?

items.speaker: Soldier I
items.text: Do you have any idea what I've been through to get here?
He points toward the Foundation symbol adorning the counter with a grim stare.

items.speaker: Soldier I
items.text: I spent three months in the trenches fighting Manus Vindictae for this organization. Now you're asking me to throw away what's left of my life?

items.speaker: Soldier I
items.text: And it's not just my belongings. I brought things for my little brother, too. The commander said we'd be moving again after we sign this contract. I don't see why I have to throw it all away.
Foundation security make their way over to the counter, flanking the man on both sides.

items.speaker: Foundation Security
items.text: Calm down, sir. You'll have to discard any excess baggage before we can allow you entry. No exceptions.

items.speaker: Foundation Security
items.text: We need to get you all processed quickly so you can sign your military service contracts. There's a lot of paperwork to do.
Another soldier who had arrived with him approaches.

items.speaker: Soldier II
items.text: Just do as he says, Arthur. You know these bureaucrat types. They're no different here than any back home.

items.speaker: Soldier II
items.text: Heads are too clogged up with rules and regulations. There's no talking any sense into them. Might as well save yourself the bother.
At his comrade's behest, the soldier finally parts with his belongings.

items.speaker: Soldier I
items.text: Hmph.
From the other side of the hall, a tall and lithe woman has been watching the scene unfold.
Someone else joins her.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: What are you doing here, Ms. Druvis?

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: Just looking around.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: I guess I find it odd seeing all these long lines. It's not normal to have so many people waiting to come in, especially so close to the "Storm."

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: Soon, they'll be putting on Foundation uniforms. And then, just like that, they'll be told to say goodbye to their family, friends, homelands—their entire era.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Please, Ms. Druvis, it's best we don't talk about that here. Most of those waiting in line aren't aware of this "issue."

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: They've been fighting Manus Vindictae for months. Don't you think they might have learned something from our enemies?

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: The Foundation's policy forbids revealing information on the "Storm" to any personnel from the current era. It doesn't matter what they may or may not already know.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: What is it?

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: Was that sarcasm in your voice? You find the Foundation's policy absurd too, don't you?

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: I wouldn't say that.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: Vertin told me about you. You went under deep cover in Manus Vindictae, forced yourself to become someone you're not, did things you've come to regret.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: You paid an unimaginable price to complete the Foundation's mission.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: But even now, after you've returned home, you're dissatisfied with the character you're playing.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: I can't help but wonder what the "you" you really want to be is like.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: I don't know. I've never had the time to answer that question.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: The Foundation only gave me a new role, not a new identity. They expected me to fall back into my old self.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: Are you here to check in on us? To make sure we aren't planning anything too radical?

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: You can rest assured. It won't happen.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: I appreciate it. Then, let's put it behind us. Thank you for trusting the Foundation.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: But I don't trust the Foundation. I've always doubted their ability to bring about their professed order and peace for all.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: It might be best to end our conversation here, Ms. Druvis.
Druvis ignores the suggestion.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: They bring these people in under false pretenses, knowing full well that after the "Storm" wipes out their era, they'll be isolated and moldable. And just like that, the Foundation gets a new generation of puppets.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: Uprooted, shorn down, and processed, like trees turned into logs. No one ever asks them what they want to be. They never get that chance.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: I work with the Foundation only because of Vertin. I am loyal to her, devoted to her cause. Not yours.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: I can face the uncertainty of the future because I know what I'm fighting for. How would these people react if they found out the truth?

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: Don't you think some of them would rather risk their lives to find another shelter than give up their freedom to the Foundation?

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: You mean they might want to join Manus Vindictae.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: Or the Gryphon Legion, or some other shelter we don't know of, like the Apeiron island.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: How long do you think the Foundation's policies would hold if they didn't present themselves as the only option?

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: That's a stage one alert.
A high-pitched alarm drones over their voices, blaring out from all directions.
The tone and rhythm are too rare a combination for most to immediately realize their meaning.

items.speaker: Registrar
items.text: What? What's going on now?

items.speaker: Soldier I
items.text: An assault? Or a bombardment?

items.speaker: Male Investigator
items.text: Everyone, stay calm and wait for further instructions.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: Could it be something related to the Storm Syndrome? Or another attack outside?

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Neither. A stage one alert means ...
The color drains from her face as she turns toward the Committee Building.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: A major crisis is happening inside headquarters.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Ms. Druvis, please return to Team Timekeeper and lead them to the nearest shelter.
Ms. Stranger offers a wordless goodbye and rushes off.
Warning: Stage one alert. Unidentified intruders in headquarters. Emergency evacuation procedures initiated.

items.speaker: Broadcast
items.text: All personnel are to obey ranking officers during evacuation and await further instructions in the emergency shelters.

items.speaker: Broadcast
items.text: This is not a drill. Repeat: Stage one alert. Unidentified intruders in headquarters.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: Well, well. It is of little surprise—

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: That the white fortress doth not extend its courtesy to an unbidden guest.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: Yet I shall brook no refusal.
Southern Garden, St. Pavlov Foundation

items.speaker: Ustrina
items.text: A most impressive display of strength.

items.speaker: İlmek
items.text: Look at them run. Perhaps I overdid things.

items.speaker: İlmek
items.text: *sigh* I wish I didn't have to be so rough with them.

items.speaker: Ustrina
items.text: Guiding One.
The followers watch as their deity approaches the Committee Building in slow, deft steps.

items.speaker: Taira
items.text: How has our ambush against the Foundation's Response Squad proceeded?

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: They've been taken care of.

items.speaker: Taira
items.text: Hm. Impressive. Then I need only point my blade forward.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: Heh, bringing a knife to a gunfight. You are a hoot.
Krutov turns his gaze from the shell covered in warped patterns and toward his troops.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: Assault squads, lock down the first floor of the Committee Building. Eliminate any resistance.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: We'll demolish their tower and rip the guts from these arrogant hypocrites!

items.speaker: Manus Soldier I
items.text: Yes, sir!
Hallway, St. Pavlov Foundation

items.speaker: Foundation Staff Member I
items.text: Run!

items.speaker: Foundation Staff Member II
items.text: It's Manus Vindictae! I saw them!
A white figure brushes past her as the sounds of gunshots and incantations reverberate through the crowded corridor.
The footsteps grow sparser. It's time to go. She shouldn't push against the flow of the crowd anymore.
You ...

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: Ms. Stranger raises her head.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: Grace, a moth sealed inside a human's cage.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Arcana? No, this can't be happening.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: You need not fear. I come only seeking an answer. We have no dark designs.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: To speak thy name doth please me still, and I do not forget the deeds thou once didst for us, grieved though I am by thy betrayal.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: Come hither, child. For I carry a gift that should have long ago been bestowed upon thee.
